# Hegemony and Germany – An odd couple

By Joachim Schild

Book Discussing Pax Germanica

Edition 1st Edition

First Published 2024

Imprint Routledge

Pages 16

eBook ISBN 9781003491224

Share

## ABSTRACT

This contribution takes issue with the interpretation of Germany as a hegemon in regional integration. It stresses that power diffusion and sharing between the institutions of the European Union and between its member states is the name of the game in the highly institutionalised and power-taming environment of the European Union, not hegemony of a single member state. This contribution clarifies its understanding of the concepts of hegemony, leadership, and dominance. Thereafter, it uses the eurozone and the COVID-19 crises as critical test cases. The article shows that Germany dominated on some issues during the management of the eurozone crisis and the reform of its governance architecture and acted occasionally as a co-leader with France during this crisis and later when dealing with the economic impact of the COVID-19 crisis. During the war in Ukraine, however, it found itself rather in a follower role on the key issue of providing heavy weapons to Ukraine for its self-defence, notably during the first year of the war. These crises since the early 2010s in the economic and security realm provide us with little empirical evidence of a hegemonic position and role of Germany in the European Union.
